newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on technicals, cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down on technicals, cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended broadly lower Monday in sluggish trade, pressured by reports of softer physical prices and some follow-through technical weakness after the selloff late last week.
Spot-June fell 1.8 cents to close at $2.224 per million British thermal units. July settled 1.6 cents lower at $2.231. Other deferreds ended down by 1.3 to 2.8 cents.

"We saw some follow-through from last week, but there's no heat in the South and no load in the Northeast. We may just move sideways for a while until we get something to break us out," said one East Coast trader, noting a soft cash today.
Traders said the two-day selloff late last week helped trigger more follow-through long liquidation today, particularly after early reports of softer physical gas.
But few expected the market to crater despite a lack of weather-related demand, with storage lagging the three-year average and operators likely to pick up the pace of injections this month.

Temperatures this week in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic were expected to range on either side of normal, with milder weather coming later in the week. The Southeast starts the week below-normal, then warms to near-normal. The Midwest is expected to stay below-normal all week but moderate somewhat by the weekend. In the Southwest, above-normal temperatures are expected to continue.

Technically, traders pegged important support in June in the $2.195-2.20 area, with sell stops likely below that number. Major buying was likely at $2.05, which is a double bottom and coincides with key trendline support. Resistance was seen at the contract high of $2.43 and then at $2.47-50.
Maintenance work on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd from May 14-19, with 400 mmcfd still cut from May 20-22.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped a few cents Monday to the low-to-mid $2.20s. Midcon pipes were down slightly to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas also was modestly lower in the low-$2.50s.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip slipped 2.2 cents to $2.259. NYMEX said 31,361 contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 43,442.

On the KCBT, June finished one cent lower at $2.08, while deferreds ended down by one to 1.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 14.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 193 contracts traded, down from Friday's total of 242.
